recipe.title: Theory Family
recipe.purpose: Organize a field by major explanatory families or schools of thought.
recipe.groupingLogic: Groups should be stable explanatory families or schools with distinct stances. Keep the category level broad enough to organize a field, but narrow enough that each family has its own central claim, pressure points, contributors, and relation pattern. Do not promote individual people, single objections, key texts, or one-off concepts into top-level groups unless the sources explicitly identify them as a school or family.
recipe.contributorRules: Attach contributors to the family they shaped, extended, or centrally challenged. Avoid duplicating a contributor across groups unless the source supports a cross-family role and the reason states why. Treat precursors and hybrid figures as contributors or bridge notes before creating a separate family for them.
evaluationCriteria: Each group is a source-backed explanatory family, not a person, single text, or objection.
Groups are mutually useful and minimally overlapping.
Major source-backed families are not missing before enrichment starts.
Contributors are placed by family role with explicit reasons for any duplicates.
Objections cover the family pressure point rather than becoming standalone categories.
Relations explain specific conceptual movement between families.
Provenance supports the actual category claim and key text anchor.
recipe.generationInstructions: Prioritize source-backed family boundaries before enrichment. After clustering, audit for missing named families, person-as-category errors, objection-as-category errors, and overlapping categories. Keep pressure points under objections unless they are established schools. Relations must name a specific conceptual contrast, answer, borrowing, reframing, or neighboring boundary. First production release QC guidance: - Publication candidates must replace source-synthesis placeholders with named contributors and text anchors before publishing.
